summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, type 1 diabetes with functioning pancreatic transplants, and heart failure was admitted for dizziness and new-onset chest pain. She associated the dizziness with recent initiation of pregabalin, which she discontinued prior to admission. Her symptoms were complicated by supratherapeutic INR (3.8), mild hyperkalemia, and pulmonary edema. Chest pain developed during transfer and resolved with tramadol; serial troponins were mildly elevated but stable, without evidence of acute ischemia. She underwent two hemodialysis sessions, which improved fluid status, potassium, and overall symptoms. Warfarin was held and restarted at home dose, with bridging anticoagulation using enoxaparin. Dizziness resolved, and pregabalin was discontinued due to suspected side effects. She was discharged home with services, asymptomatic, on her baseline medications plus short-term Lovenox.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Heart valve replaced by other means
